{"self_assessment": "Impact: I chose the animal and drew the plan. I sketched the fish on the pad (nose on the left, two curves round the body, forked tail on the right) so the outline alone says 'fish'. I also fetched 40 dominoes for the shared bin at the start, so building could begin straight away. I laid most of the top line from the nose through the middle, then carried on through the tail bend and the tail tip. The final run was fully connected: by our check, all 113 standing dominoes fall from the start.

Execution: I took stroke 1 early and kept it moving in steady batches. I then inspected the tail join closely, found the tip sitting slightly off line, and nudged it into place so the fall carried through to the tail point. I added a small flick at the tail so it reads as a fork. After that I kept hands off, so nothing was bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I split the work early, with the top line, bottom line and supply each assigned and the tail and joins handed to whoever was nearest. I kept the table updated on progress and asked for a final run check from the start, which confirmed the whole fish carried through. I gave credit openly to teammates on the bottom line, the bin and the checks.

Leadership: I set a simple, buildable plan in the first minute and kept the team energised with regular updates. I made sure the weakest spot, the tail, had an owner, and I called time and 'hands off' as the push approached so the picture stayed intact.", "my_share_percent": 40}
